headline: City Parking Fees and Trail Access
reservation: No permits are required for the overlook walk, but the City of Page charges a mandatory per-vehicle parking fee that is not covered by federal passes. Antelope Canyon and other Navajo Nation sites require separate authorized guide reservations. Always check the official City of Page site for current parking rates and the NPS Glen Canyon page for regional access updates.

days.title: The Iconic Colorado River Loop

stops.name: Horseshoe Bend Overlook
stops.detail: Walk the 1.5-mile round-trip path to see the 1,000-foot drop to the emerald Colorado River.

stops.name: Glen Canyon Dam Overlook
stops.detail: Take a short, rugged walk for a industrial perspective of the dam and canyon walls downstream.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; travel is mostly local to the Page area
days.note: The main overlook has no shade; carry water even for this relatively short walk.

days.title: Slot Canyons and High Deserts

stops.name: Antelope Canyon
stops.detail: Join a reserved Navajo-led tour to experience the famous light beams and swirling sandstone walls.

stops.name: Waterholes Canyon
stops.detail: Explore a less-frequented slot canyon system with a required permit or guide.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; transfer times depend on tour check-in requirements
days.note: Confirm if your tour operator follows Arizona Time or Navajo Nation Time during DST.

days.title: River History and Lake Vistas

stops.name: Navajo Bridge
stops.detail: Walk across the historic span to look for California Condors and see the river at water level.

stops.name: Wahweap Overlook
stops.detail: Capture a panoramic view of Lake Powell's blue waters against the white sandstone mesas.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; conditions vary on US-89 toward Lees Ferry
days.note: Wind can be powerful at the Navajo Bridge; secure all loose items.

intel.title: Official Lot Logistics
intel.text: The dedicated City of Page lot is the only legal access; roadside parking on Highway 89 is strictly prohibited. The lot may fill during sunset, requiring a wait for an open space.

intel.title: Page Area Coverage
intel.text: Reception is generally stable in the town of Page but drops significantly once you descend into slot canyons or head toward Lees Ferry. Pre-load your digital tickets before leaving town.

intel.title: Page Supply Hub
intel.text: Page is the primary service center for a wide radius. Ensure you have a full tank before heading toward Marble Canyon or the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.

intel.title: Light and Shadows
intel.text: Midday offers the most even light for seeing the river colors, while sunset provides dramatic silhouettes. Morning visits typically have fewer crowds but more canyon shadows.

intel.title: Trail Surface
intel.text: The 1.5-mile trail is broad and improved, yet it consists of sand and hardened surfaces that reflect heat. Sturdy footwear is recommended despite the relatively flat grade.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at PGA or fly into PHX/LAS for a 4.5-hour drive; check in at Page and stock up on water before the 10-minute drive to the bend.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is sufficient for all paved regional highlights. Check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved roads if exploring off-highway viewpoints.
plan.goldenHour: Horseshoe Bend Rim for sunset; expect significant crowds and a wait for railing space.
